scenarioStory.history: Onset of epigastric burning and mid-back discomfort approximately 45 minutes prior to EMS arrival while eating dinner; associated diaphoresis, nausea, and mild dyspnea. Patient initially attributed symptoms to heartburn and took antacids without relief. Denies classic substernal chest pressure or radiation to the left arm.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Patient is alert and conversant, complaining of epigastric burning and mid-back discomfort he attributes to indigestion. He is diaphoretic, pale, and mildly tachypneic. Nothing about the presentation screams 'chest pain,' which is exactly the trap of a posterior STEMI equivalent. → Posterior STEMI recognized: Posterior STEMI equivalent confirmed; crew proceeds with STEMI protocol treatment and hospital notification. → STEMI activated, transport to PCI center: Patient packaged for transport; repeat 12-lead performed en route showing persistent posterior injury pattern; hospital catheterization lab activated.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is alert and conversant, complaining of epigastric burning and mid-back discomfort he attributes to indigestion. He is diaphoretic, pale, and mildly tachypneic. Nothing about the presentation screams 'chest pain,' which is exactly the trap of a posterior STEMI equivalent.
relatedChecklist: Perform focused history/physical; recognize atypical anginal-equivalent symptoms (epigastric/back pain, diaphoresis) as possible ACS
Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact

scenarioEvents.name: Posterior STEMI recognized
scenarioEvents.description: Posterior STEMI equivalent confirmed; crew proceeds with STEMI protocol treatment and hospital notification.
relatedChecklist: Obtain posterior leads (V7-V9); initial EKG is non-diagnostic in appearance but suspicious
Activate STEMI system of care; give advance notification to receiving PCI-capable hospital
Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL (SBP 122 mmHg, above 100 mmHg threshold); may repeat q3-5 min; screened negative for PDE5 inhibitor use
Continue cardiac monitoring; watch for dysrhythmias or clinical deterioration

scenarioEvents.name: STEMI activated, transport to PCI center
scenarioEvents.description: Patient packaged for transport; repeat 12-lead performed en route showing persistent posterior injury pattern; hospital catheterization lab activated.
relatedChecklist: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs en route; reassess for interval changes
Provide early notification to receiving facility of any changes in patient condition or serial EKGs
Fentanyl 95 mcg IV (95 kg x 1 mcg/kg = 95 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg) for discomfort unresponsive to nitrates

scenarioEvents.name: Posterior STEMI missed
scenarioEvents.description: Without recognition of the posterior STEMI pattern, the patient's ongoing ischemia worsens over the next several minutes; discomfort intensifies and he becomes more diaphoretic and anxious.

scenarioEvents.name: VF arrest - missed STEMI
scenarioEvents.description: Cardiac arrest secondary to acute ischemia; crew must immediately recognize arrest and begin high-quality CPR with defibrillation.
relatedChecklist: Recognize cardiac arrest; begin immediate high-quality chest compressions
Defibrillate at 120 J (Zoll biphasic) as soon as VF is confirmed
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO push (95 kg x 0.1 mg/kg = 9.5 mg, capped at protocol max 1 mg)
Resume chest compressions immediately post-shock without a pulse check, for 2 minutes
